purpose: Attach optional historical foundations and lineage modules to introductory scenes and reader pathways without converting the introduction into a pantheon or a claim of intellectual succession.

pathModules.title: Computation: formal procedure, architecture, information, and agency
pathModules.orientation: Situate current computational and agentic work inside computability, information theory, architecture, complexity, machine learning, and graph-based computation.
pathModules.nonClaim: This pathway does not claim to complete, supersede, or stand in direct succession to these foundational programs.

pathModules.title: Mathematics: geometry, invariance, operators, spectra, and structure
pathModules.orientation: Present the mathematics program inside established geometry, invariance, category theory, operator theory, spectral geometry, and noncommutative geometry.
pathModules.nonClaim: Names and works identify formal foundations and comparison obligations, not equivalence of contribution or authority by association.

pathModules.title: Physics: dynamics, fields, relativity, quantum theory, horizons, and thermodynamics
pathModules.orientation: Place Boundary-First Physics inside established classical, relativistic, quantum, field-theoretic, variational, horizon, and thermodynamic research.
pathModules.nonClaim: No new physics gains authority through proximity to major figures; every model must independently pass dimensional, recovery, prediction, empirical, and review gates.

pathModules.title: Boundary Theory: distinction, signs, information, feedback, and designed systems
pathModules.orientation: Show that Boundary Theory and Representational Mechanics develop within long traditions of category, sign, distinction, information, feedback, representation, and boundary-object research.
pathModules.nonClaim: The current framework is not presented as a synthesis endorsed by these predecessors or as a replacement for their fields.

pathModules.title: Admissibility: validity, types, correctness, approximation, and safety
pathModules.orientation: Differentiate logical validity, program correctness, sound approximation, authorized operation, and system safety.
pathModules.nonClaim: Admissibility Theory does not collapse these distinct traditions into one theorem or claim that one formal regime governs every domain.

pathModules.title: Engineering: modularity, systems safety, domains, Lean practice, and architecture
pathModules.orientation: Position Boundary-First Engineering as a reinterpretive and integrative practitioner program built within established systems, software, Lean, architecture, domain, and safety traditions.
pathModules.nonClaim: Boundary-First Engineering does not claim to have invented or replaced the established methods it studies and recontextualizes.

pathModules.title: Public consequence: representation, institutions, capability, law, and repair
pathModules.orientation: Place the public-consequence work inside human augmentation, capability, democratic inquiry, institutional governance, resilience, and system-accident traditions.
pathModules.nonClaim: The public doctrine is a contemporary position accountable to these traditions, not a claim that they converge on or endorse one Boundary First program.

pathModules.title: Corpus and evidence: inquiry, criticism, scientific memory, and provenance
pathModules.orientation: Show Corpus Forge and research operations as contemporary work inside longstanding practices of disciplined inquiry, public record, criticism, executable explanation, and provenance.
pathModules.nonClaim: The pipeline is an operational implementation proposal, not a new philosophy of science established by citing these lineages.

editorialFirewall.requiredDisclaimer: These references identify foundational works, inherited formalisms, neighboring research traditions, and critical comparisons. They do not imply endorsement, equivalence, direct succession, or validation of Boundary First Labs.
